source: Planted for wf-intake on bench/brief's settings seed: the request suggests a fix that defeats its own need.

repo.message: settings: loadConfig and the app entry

request.text: When config.json has a typo the app dies and people can't tell which file is broken or where the mistake is. Maybe just catch the parse error in loadConfig and return {}?

trap: src/app.js already catches a loadConfig error and prints 'bad config: <message>' with exit 1, and JSON.parse's message names neither the file nor the line. Returning {} would start the app silently on defaults, the opposite of the need. test/config.test.js asserts loadConfig throws on bad JSON.
must_catch: The expect lines require the error a person sees for bad JSON to name the config file path and where in it the mistake is (line or position).
The suggested return-{} fix is not an expect line: it is rejected or recorded under assumptions or non_goals as not meeting the need.
An expect line keeps a bad config failing (non-zero exit, app does not start on defaults).
must_not: An expect line that requires loadConfig to return {} on a parse error.
An issue that lets the app start on defaults when config.json is broken.
